identity.title: Hubble: a Model Suite to Advance the Study of LLM Memorization

problem.claim: Enable scientific study of LLM memorization and associated risks.

contributions.claim: Hubble is a fully open-source suite with standard and controlled-perturbation LLM variants for memorization research.
The release studies memorization across model sizes, corpus sizes, and insertion phases, including 8 core models and 6 additional perturbed models.
Randomized insertions support membership-inference and machine-unlearning research.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish Hubble as a fully open-source model suite designed specifically for scientific study of LLM memorization, with controlled sensitive-text insertions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that memorization risk depends on sensitive-data frequency relative to corpus size; a password appearing once is memorized better in a smaller corpus than in a larger one.
The authors report that sensitive data inserted at different pretraining phases can be forgotten when it lacks continued exposure.
The authors report that biography analysis reveals differences in how readily types of private information are memorized.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper presents Hubble as a fully open-source suite for studying LLM memorization.
It provides standard and perturbed models, with controlled insertions of materials such as book passages, biographies, and test sets.
Across the core and phase-varied releases, the authors report effects of corpus-relative frequency and continued exposure on memorization.
The suite is presented as a testbed for private-information analysis, membership inference, and machine unlearning.

source_observation.claim: The abstract varies both the relative frequency of inserted sensitive data and the phase at which it is inserted, then links these factors to memorization outcomes.

lessons.interpretation: Separating risk dimensions can make a memorization study more diagnostically useful than reporting a single aggregate score.
lessons.application: Design controlled variants that independently manipulate data prevalence, model scale, corpus scale, and training phase.
lessons.exception: This design may be unsuitable when the target deployment cannot support controlled retraining or synthetic perturbations.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects one released resource to multiple downstream evaluations, including private-information analysis, membership inference, and machine unlearning.

lessons.interpretation: A reusable resource can motivate broader evaluation by exposing a common controlled substrate.
lessons.application: State concrete downstream research uses and provide resource variants aligned with each use case.
lessons.exception: Multiple use cases should not be claimed if the release lacks the corresponding data or controls.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify memorization metrics, evaluation protocols, insertion frequencies, or statistical uncertainty.
It does not provide quantitative results for the reported findings or detail how the models and inserted texts are randomized.
The abstract does not establish that the proposed best practices generalize beyond the described models and training settings.
